jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Moran Company is pleased to partner with Friends of the Children - Stockton to recruit the organization's next Executive Director.

Friends of the Children is a nationally recognized nonprofit organization with a powerful mission to impact generational change by empowering youth who face the greatest obstacles through relationships with paid professional mentors—12+ years, no matter what. For more than three decades, the Friends of the Children model has produced measurable outcomes for children and families across the country. Friends of the Children’s impact is evident - a longitudinal study by the Harvard Business School Association of Oregon confirmed that for every $1 invested in Friends of the Children, the community benefits over $7 in saved social costs.

Established in 2024, Friends of the Children - Stockton has been building the infrastructure, partnerships, and organizational capacity to support sustainable growth in its mission. The chapter has a strong foundation in place, including strong seed funding (approximately $1.7 million in fundraising revenue last year), a dedicated and mission-driven staff team of five, an engaged seven-member Board of Directors, and the collaborative support of a proven national network, including operational, financial, programmatic, and leadership resources. The chapter is poised to accelerate its visibility, expand its impact, and strengthen its position as a leading force for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The Executive Director role is an incredible opportunity to build upon this momentum, helping establish Friends of the Children - Stockton as one of the region's most visible, trusted, and influential organizations serving children and families through its two-generation approach.

Friends of the Children – Stockton seeks a highly relational, entrepreneurial, and community-centered Executive Director to guide the organization through its next phase of start-up growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors and partnering with Friends of the Children National, the Executive Director will serve as the organization’s chief executive, fundraiser, strategist, ambassador, and culture-builder. This leader will focus on expanding visibility, increasing philanthropic investment, strengthening community partnerships, building organizational capacity, and advancing long-term outcomes for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The successful candidate will be a compelling advocate and storyteller who can build authentic relationships with donors, community leaders, partners, staff, families, and other stakeholders. This is an ideal opportunity for an accomplished nonprofit executive who combines strategic vision, entrepreneurial business acumen, and hands-on leadership with a deep commitment to mission.

The Executive Director will provide strategic, mission-centered leadership while serving as the organization’s lead fundraiser, spokesperson, ambassador, and advocate. This leader will partner closely with the Board, National leadership, staff, and peer Executive Directors to strengthen governance, support collaboration, and ensure fidelity to the Friends of the Children model. They will lead fundraising and community relations efforts by cultivating donors, foundations, corporations, public officials, and nonprofit partners to build a diversified and sustainable funding base. The Executive Director will oversee strategic planning, annual operations, budgeting, growth initiatives, performance monitoring, and risk management to advance long-term organizational goals. They will also ensure high-quality program delivery, sound financial stewardship, strong administrative systems, and a supportive team culture that promotes staff development, accountability, morale, and retention.

The ideal candidate will have a bachelor’s degree, with an advanced degree preferred, and 10 or more years of progressively responsible executive leadership experience in nonprofit or related environments. They should bring demonstrated success in fundraising, operations, finance, strategy, people leadership, organizational growth, and major gift development, along with strong executive presence and credibility with donors, board members, community leaders, and public stakeholders. The successful candidate will be a strategic, collaborative, culturally competent, and approachable leader with excellent communication, storytelling, decision-making, and supervisory skills, as well as a strong commitment to child development, youth outcomes, and long-term mentoring models.

The salary range for this position is $145,000–$165,000 including incentive compensation, depending on qualifications and experience. Friends of the Children offers a comprehensive benefits package and a culture that values collaboration, belonging, professional growth, and work-life harmony.

The search for the Friends of the Children - Stockton Executive Director is being conducted by The Moran Company. Questions about the position can be directed to Angie Heer, The Moran Company: angie (at) morancompany.com.

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to Angie Heer at The Moran Company via the secure online portal. The resume should include all professional education and experience, examples of nonprofit leadership accomplishments, dates of employment (month and year), position/title, and organization names. The cover letter should highlight your relevant experience, passion for Friends of the Children Stockton’s mission, and your approach to building and scaling an organization. Applications should be submitted by July 19.

Sarah House Santa Barbara provides end-of-life care with extraordinary kindness
to people with low incomes and individuals living with HIV/AIDS. Our 8-bed residential home offers social model hospice care in a compassionate, dignified environment during life's final chapter.

For over three decades, Sarah House has been a sanctuary for our community's most vulnerable residents, ensuring that no one faces death alone or without comfort. We work in partnership with hospice providers, community organizations, and dedicated volunteers to deliver person-centered care grounded in respect, warmth, and humanity.

Position Overview

Sarah House seeks a passionate, skillful, strategic, mission-driven leader to serve as Executive Director / Development Director. The ideal candidate will bring proven nonprofit management experience, fundraising expertise, and a deep commitment to serving those experiencing homelessness, serious illness, and end-of-life transitions.

The Executive Director / Development Director, reports to and works with the Board of Directors, providing overall leadership, strategic planning, legal compliance, and operational supervision for the organization, in accordance with all Federal, State, Local and Licensing Regulations and Company Policy and Procedures. This role requires extensive fundraising and development work with financial oversight, board relations, community engagement, and staff supervision—all while keeping Sarah House's mission of extraordinary kindness at the center of every decision.

audit processes
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Proficiency with nonprofit financial and donor management systems (QuickBooks,

- 5% Commission associated with Grants and Fund Raising performance

The Executive Director / Development Director works primarily from a home office or on site working space, with regular visits to Sarah House facility, community meetings, donor visits, and external appointments. Some evening and weekend work required for fundraising events and board meetings. This role requires comfort working in a residential hospice environment.

Friends of the Children–San Diego is launching with extraordinary momentum. Rather than building from scratch, the organization's first Executive Director will inherit a remarkable opportunity to accelerate an already well-established vision. Friends of the Children–San Diego seeks a highly relational, entrepreneurial, and community-centered Executive Director to lead the successful launch and long-term growth of this new chapter. About San Diego Health Connect

San Diego Health Connect (SDHC) is a nonprofit Health Information Exchange (HIE) and designated California Qualified Health Information Organization (QHIO) serving San Diego and Imperial Counties. As a subsidiary of 211 San Diego, SDHC serves as a trusted bridge between healthcare, public health, emergency medical services, behavioral health, and community-based organizations, enabling secure, real-time exchange of health information to improve care coordination and advance whole-person care. Processing more than 50 million clinical messages each month and maintaining a patient index of 4.8 million individuals, SDHC connects hospitals, health systems, federally qualified health centers (FQHCs), physician groups, EMS agencies, public health departments, managed care organizations, pharmacies, and community partners throughout the region. Through leadership in interoperability, health information exchange, and healthcare innovation, SDHC supports improved health outcomes while advancing California's vision for integrated health and social care.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the President & CEO of 211 San Diego, the Executive Director (ED) provides strategic, operational, financial, and technical leadership for San Diego Health Connect. As the organization's senior executive, the ED is responsible for advancing SDHC's mission while ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, financial sustainability, and continued growth as one of California's premier Health Information Exchanges.

Responsibilities

Develop and execute SDHC's strategic plan, business model, and long-term financial sustainability roadmap.
Translate organizational vision into measurable operational objectives, ensuring successful execution across all areas of the organization.
Identify opportunities to leverage SDHC's relationship with 211 San Diego to expand partnerships, strengthen interoperability, and increase organizational impact throughout the healthcare and social care ecosystem.

Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, service excellence, and mission-driven leadership.

Represent SDHC in local, regional, state, and national healthcare interoperability initiatives and policy discussions.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with healthcare executives, elected officials, state agencies, industry associations, and community leaders.
Monitor, interpret, and synthesize healthcare legislation, public policy, and regulatory developments affecting health information exchange, interoperability, healthcare technology, and data sharing.
Guide organizational strategy related to California's Data Exchange Framework (DxF), TEFCA, Qualified Health Information Organization (QHIO) requirements, CMS regulations, HIPAA, HITECH, and emerging interoperability standards.
Provide executive oversight of all organizational operations, ensuring high-quality, efficient, and compliant delivery of HIE services.
Oversee budgeting, procurement, contract management, operational planning, and organizational performance measurement.
Provide strategic leadership over SDHC's technical infrastructure.
Ensure operational excellence while maintaining the flexibility to pivot quickly in response to evolving healthcare priorities, regulatory changes, funding opportunities, and technological advancements.
Build, strengthen, and sustain trusted executive-level partnerships with various stakeholders.
Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable federal, state, and industry regulations.

Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team of approximately 10–15 professionals across operations, technology, data services, and administration.

Munchausen by Proxy (MBP) is a serious, complex, and widely misunderstood form of medical child abuse. It leaves a wide swath of destruction and trauma for everyone involved, often resulting in lifelong devastation for survivors.

Founded in 2021 in collaboration with some of the world’s top experts on MBP, the Munchausen Support Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to providing science- and fact-based resources. The Foundation offers critical support for family members in crisis, survivors seeking treatment, and professionals navigating active cases.

Today, the organization offers structured 10-week survivor support groups alongside specialized cohorts, including dedicated groups for fathers and grandparents. In addition to direct peer support, the Munchausen Support Foundation focuses on pioneering research, education for healthcare providers on how to recognize medical abuse, and professional training for proper evaluation and support delivery.

As the Foundation approaches its 5-year milestone, the Board of Directors is seeking a high-caliber, experienced, and visionary leader with a growth mindset to serve as its inaugural Executive Director. This pivotal role is designed for a strategic builder who will guide the organization through its next phase of expansion to deliver deeper, wider support to those impacted by Munchausen by Proxy. The Executive Director will work closely with the Board of Directors to develop and execute strategic and operational plans that expand the Foundation’s reach, impact, and organizational capacity. This leader will supervise volunteers, board members, and paid consultants while ensuring strong daily operations and full legal, ethical, and regulatory compliance. The Executive Director will support founders and board members as public representatives of the organization, strengthen brand awareness through multimedia and digital communications, deepen relationships with partners, donors, healthcare professionals, and institutional stakeholders, and oversee peer support groups, research initiatives, and specialized committees. This role will also lead annual fundraising strategy, manage the Foundation’s budget, support long-term financial sustainability, and partner with the Board Treasurer to provide clear financial reporting to the Board and key stakeholders.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong commitment to the mission of the Munchausen Support Foundation, exceptional emotional intelligence, trauma-informed sensitivity, and the ability to communicate complex medical and social issues with clarity to diverse audiences. CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

SPY is looking for a leader who can guide an established youth homelessness organization through its next stage of scale, sustainability, housing growth, public advocacy, and strategic planning. The next leader must have an unwavering commitment to championing SPY's mission and the young people it serves; the ability to adaptively support and develop SPY staff; effectively lead a robust fundraising, external relations, and finance management strategy; and the experience to oversee a complex $15M organization operating 24 hour programs.

ABOUT SAFE PLACE FOR YOUTH

Safe Place for Youth is a leading youth homelessness organization serving young people ages 12 to 25 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Los Angeles. SPY’s mission is to prevent and end youth homelessness through supportive services, sustainable housing opportunities, community collaboration, and advocacy, with a vision of a socially just and equitable world where all young people are empowered to thrive in self-directed lives and have a safe place to call home.

SPY provides a continuum of youth-centered services that includes street outreach, a drop-in center, case management, education and employment, health and wellness, healing arts, community garden, pregnant and parenting support, shelter, social enterprise, family reunification, housing, and advocacy. In 2025, SPY served more than 1,200 youth, helped 315 young people move into housing, and connected hundreds more to mental health counseling, case management, workforce training, creative arts, street outreach, and other critical supports.

SPY has entered a new stage of organizational complexity and opportunity. The organization now operates 10 sites across the County, including multiple housing programs across shelter, transitional housing, and permanent housing, providing 224 housing resources on any given night. SPY also provides robust supportive services through a field-based model and out of our drop-in center in Venice, including basic needs resources, case management, mental health, substance use counseling, education and employment, pregnant and parenting, healing arts and more.       

The next leader will be called upon to sustain operational excellence across housing and services programs, actively lead a robust fundraising strategy, ensure strong financial oversight, continue SPY’s leadership in advocacy, maintain strong community collaboration, support strong recruitment, retention and development of staff, while keeping the dignity and wellbeing of youth at the center of all of SPY’s work.     

POSITION OVERVIEW

SPY seeks a Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization into its next phase of impact, sustainability, and public leadership.

The next leader will inherit a respected, mission-driven organization with a strong community identity, a seasoned senior team, an engaged Board, a growing housing portfolio, a newly redeveloped drop-in center, a planned capital campaign, and an urgent opportunity to shape the future of youth homelessness policy and practice in Los Angeles. The role requires a leader who can hold multiple responsibilities at once: stewarding a complex nonprofit enterprise, strengthening internal systems, serving as an external advocate and fundraiser, leading through a new strategic plan, and ensuring that SPY remains deeply connected to the young people and communities it serves.

The successful candidate will be a values-driven, emotionally intelligent, operationally capable, and externally credible leader who can balance ambition with sustainability. They will bring the strategic judgment to decide where SPY should grow, where it should consolidate, where it should advocate, and where it should say no. They will be equally comfortable with youth, staff, donors, elected officials, public agency leaders, community partners, and the Board.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute strategic plans in alignment with the organization’s mission, vision, and values. Lead the organization in identifying trends, funding environment, challenges, and future growth opportunities in the housing environment.
Advocacy and Policy Engagement: Serve as an external champion, advocate, and coalition builder for SPY. Build and maintain strong relationships with elected officials, public agencies, funders, community stakeholders, peer organizations, housing partners, researchers, advocates, neighborhood leaders, and media. Advocate for youth-specific homelessness funding, policy, housing resources, and service models.

About Sarasota Polo Club

Sarasota Polo Club is a distinctive sports, entertainment, and event destination located in Sarasota, Florida. Set on more than 170 acres, the property is home to an established seasonal polo program that attracts thousands of spectators, members, players, sponsors, and guests throughout the season.

While polo remains central to the identity and heritage of the Club, Sarasota Polo Club has significant opportunity to expand the use of its property, facilities, audience, and brand beyond traditional polo operations. Ownership’s vision is to develop the Club into a broader year-round destination for sports, entertainment, hospitality, corporate, community, and special events while preserving the character and quality that make the property unique.

We are seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial leader who can operate today’s business while helping build what Sarasota Polo Club can become.

The Role

The General Manager / Chief Operating Officer will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day business and operations of Sarasota Polo Club and will work directly with ownership to execute the Club’s long-term strategy.

This is not simply a club management position. We are looking for a hands-on business leader who combines strong operational discipline with commercial instincts and an ability to identify and develop new revenue opportunities.

The successful candidate will oversee club operations, events, facilities, personnel, budgets, vendor relationships, guest experience, and coordination of the seasonal polo program. Equally important, this individual will help expand the Club’s commercial potential through non-polo events, partnerships, sponsorships, hospitality programs, facility utilization, and other revenue-producing opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead the overall day-to-day operation of Sarasota Polo Club, with accountability for operating performance, service standards, staffing, and execution.
* Develop annual operating plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures, and financial controls.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team responsible for events, facilities, grounds, hospitality, polo operations, marketing, and administration.
* Oversee the planning and execution of polo matches, major events, private functions, and other activities held on the property.
* Identify and develop opportunities to increase revenue and year-round utilization of the Club’s property and facilities.
* Build relationships with event producers, promoters, sponsors, corporate partners, vendors, community organizations, and other potential business partners.
* Evaluate new events and commercial opportunities based on revenue potential, operational requirements, brand fit, and profitability.
* Negotiate and manage vendor, tenant, promoter, and partner relationships.
* Maintain high standards for facilities, grounds, safety, security, regulatory compliance, and guest experience.
* Establish operating systems, reporting, accountability, and processes appropriate for a growing organization.
* Work closely with ownership on strategic initiatives, capital improvements, property development, and the long-term evolution of Sarasota Polo Club.

Candidate Profile

We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully managed complex venues or businesses where operations, events, hospitality, and revenue generation intersect.

Relevant backgrounds may include sports and entertainment venues, major event facilities, destination attractions, equestrian facilities, private clubs, hospitality businesses, festivals, fairgrounds, convention or event centers, or other multi-use properties.

Polo experience is not required.

The strongest candidates will demonstrate:

* Significant leadership experience with responsibility for people, operations, budgets, and financial results.
* A track record of improving business performance and developing new revenue opportunities.
* Experience managing events, venues, hospitality operations, or businesses with significant guest attendance.
* Strong financial and business judgment, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control, and P&L accountability.
* Experience recruiting, leading, developing, and holding teams accountable.
* Ability to manage multiple departments, vendors, partners, and stakeholders simultaneously.
* Strong commercial instincts and the ability to turn ideas, facilities, audiences, and partnerships into profitable business opportunities.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
* A practical, hands-on leadership style and willingness to be highly visible throughout the operation.
* Comfort working in an event-driven environment that includes weekends and holidays during the polo season.

A bachelor’s degree in business, hospitality, sports management, or a related discipline is preferred, although substantial relevant leadership experience may substitute for formal education.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to lead an established Sarasota institution through its next stage of development.

The successful candidate will inherit a substantial operating platform, recognized brand, established polo program, significant physical property, and loyal audience—but will also have the opportunity to help shape a much larger business.

We are looking for someone who sees a polo club today and can envision—and build—the sports, entertainment, hospitality, and event destination it can become.

Friends of the Children is a nationally recognized nonprofit organization with a powerful mission to impact generational change by empowering youth who face the greatest obstacles through relationships with paid professional mentors—12+ years, no matter what. For more than three decades, the Friends of the Children model has produced measurable outcomes for children and families across the country. Established in 2024, Friends of the Children - Stockton has been building the infrastructure, partnerships, and organizational capacity to support sustainable growth in its mission. The chapter has a strong foundation in place, including strong seed funding (approximately $1.7 million in fundraising revenue last year), a dedicated and mission-driven staff team of five, an engaged seven-member Board of Directors, and the collaborative support of a proven national network, including operational, financial, programmatic, and leadership resources. The chapter is poised to accelerate its visibility, expand its impact, and strengthen its position as a leading force for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The Executive Director role is an incredible opportunity to build upon this momentum, helping establish Friends of the Children - Stockton as one of the region's most visible, trusted, and influential organizations serving children and families through its two-generation approach.

Friends of the Children – Stockton seeks a highly relational, entrepreneurial, and community-centered Executive Director to guide the organization through its next phase of start-up growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors and partnering with Friends of the Children National, the Executive Director will serve as the organization’s chief executive, fundraiser, strategist, ambassador, and culture-builder. This leader will focus on expanding visibility, increasing philanthropic investment, strengthening community partnerships, building organizational capacity, and advancing long-term outcomes for children and families throughout Stockton and San Joaquin County. The successful candidate will be a compelling advocate and storyteller who can build authentic relationships with donors, community leaders, partners, staff, families, and other stakeholders. This is an ideal opportunity for an accomplished nonprofit executive who combines strategic vision, entrepreneurial business acumen, and hands-on leadership with a deep commitment to mission.

ABOUT SAFE PLACE FOR YOUTH

Safe Place for Youth is a leading youth homelessness organization serving young people ages 12 to 25 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Los Angeles. SPY has entered a new stage of organizational complexity and opportunity. The organization now operates 10 sites across the County, including multiple housing programs across shelter, transitional housing, and permanent housing, providing 224 housing resources on any given night. Oversee the growth and development of districtwide comprehensive school counseling services, including directly supervising and evaluating district team members and indirectly supporting site-based counselors.
Provide leadership and administrative direction to assigned staff for the operations, financial, and personnel resources to effectively support counseling and district goals.
Facilitate communication and collaboration among assigned departmental personnel and school and district administrators to enhance program development, service delivery, and student/family engagement.
Participate on a cross-functional team, including internal and external partners, to advance the districts’ vision of a graduate and aligned college, career, and life readiness strategies.

Provide professional learning to site- and district-based administrators to support the appropriate use of counseling staff in alignment with site-based goals.
Support school leaders to provide effective supervision and evaluative feedback to school counselors
Increase the quality and scope of the district’s counseling program by staying current in best practices and pedagogy at the state and national levels.
Work with the district’s Postsecondary team to design and execute annual My Career & Academic Plan (MyCAP) professional learning for school counselors.

Partnership Support

Build relationships with university pre-service counseling programs to attract, onboard and support graduate student interns across all BPS schools and diploma granting programs.
Build and support relationships with transition support services such as STRIVE, Massachusetts Rehabilitation Commission, and Easter Seals College Navigator.

Participate on internal and external cross-functional teams to drive the district’s college and career readiness strategies, including New Skills Boston, Success Boston and others.

new_jobs.description:
About Sarasota Polo Club

Sarasota Polo Club is a distinctive sports, entertainment, and event destination located in Sarasota, Florida. Set on more than 170 acres, the property is home to an established seasonal polo program that attracts thousands of spectators, members, players, sponsors, and guests throughout the season.

While polo remains central to the identity and heritage of the Club, Sarasota Polo Club has significant opportunity to expand the use of its property, facilities, audience, and brand beyond traditional polo operations. Ownership’s vision is to develop the Club into a broader year-round destination for sports, entertainment, hospitality, corporate, community, and special events while preserving the character and quality that make the property unique.

We are seeking an experienced, entrepreneurial leader who can operate today’s business while helping build what Sarasota Polo Club can become.

The Role

The General Manager / Chief Operating Officer will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day business and operations of Sarasota Polo Club and will work directly with ownership to execute the Club’s long-term strategy.

This is not simply a club management position. We are looking for a hands-on business leader who combines strong operational discipline with commercial instincts and an ability to identify and develop new revenue opportunities.

The successful candidate will oversee club operations, events, facilities, personnel, budgets, vendor relationships, guest experience, and coordination of the seasonal polo program. Equally important, this individual will help expand the Club’s commercial potential through non-polo events, partnerships, sponsorships, hospitality programs, facility utilization, and other revenue-producing opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead the overall day-to-day operation of Sarasota Polo Club, with accountability for operating performance, service standards, staffing, and execution.
* Develop annual operating plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures, and financial controls.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team responsible for events, facilities, grounds, hospitality, polo operations, marketing, and administration.
* Oversee the planning and execution of polo matches, major events, private functions, and other activities held on the property.
* Identify and develop opportunities to increase revenue and year-round utilization of the Club’s property and facilities.
* Build relationships with event producers, promoters, sponsors, corporate partners, vendors, community organizations, and other potential business partners.
* Evaluate new events and commercial opportunities based on revenue potential, operational requirements, brand fit, and profitability.
* Negotiate and manage vendor, tenant, promoter, and partner relationships.
* Maintain high standards for facilities, grounds, safety, security, regulatory compliance, and guest experience.
* Establish operating systems, reporting, accountability, and processes appropriate for a growing organization.
* Work closely with ownership on strategic initiatives, capital improvements, property development, and the long-term evolution of Sarasota Polo Club.

Candidate Profile

We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully managed complex venues or businesses where operations, events, hospitality, and revenue generation intersect.

Relevant backgrounds may include sports and entertainment venues, major event facilities, destination attractions, equestrian facilities, private clubs, hospitality businesses, festivals, fairgrounds, convention or event centers, or other multi-use properties.

Polo experience is not required.

The strongest candidates will demonstrate:

* Significant leadership experience with responsibility for people, operations, budgets, and financial results.
* A track record of improving business performance and developing new revenue opportunities.
* Experience managing events, venues, hospitality operations, or businesses with significant guest attendance.
* Strong financial and business judgment, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control, and P&L accountability.
* Experience recruiting, leading, developing, and holding teams accountable.
* Ability to manage multiple departments, vendors, partners, and stakeholders simultaneously.
* Strong commercial instincts and the ability to turn ideas, facilities, audiences, and partnerships into profitable business opportunities.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
* A practical, hands-on leadership style and willingness to be highly visible throughout the operation.
* Comfort working in an event-driven environment that includes weekends and holidays during the polo season.

A bachelor’s degree in business, hospitality, sports management, or a related discipline is preferred, although substantial relevant leadership experience may substitute for formal education.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to lead an established Sarasota institution through its next stage of development.

The successful candidate will inherit a substantial operating platform, recognized brand, established polo program, significant physical property, and loyal audience—but will also have the opportunity to help shape a much larger business.

We are looking for someone who sees a polo club today and can envision—and build—the sports, entertainment, hospitality, and event destination it can become.
